main_text.p: ἱμάτιον vestis, ἱματίδιον vesticula, ἱματιό- δεῖον vesticulula.
ἡ παῖς puera, (ut veteres) παιδίσκη pu- ella, παιδισκάριον puellula. Sæpe ab eodem plura: ut
λόγος fermo, λογάριον & λογίδιον fer- munculus.
κόρη puella, κορίσιον & κορίσκιον puel- lula.
παῖς, παιδίον, παιδάριον, παιδίσκος, ut La- tiné puer, puerulus, puellus, pusio: bonus, bellus, bellulus, bellatulus apud Plautum.
main_text.head: Cap.12. De parisyllaba imasculina.
main_text.p: Declinatio parisyllaba est, cujus singularis genitivus non crescit, dativusq; in diphthongum definit; accusativus in ν, cum vocali nominativi. Accusativus parisyllabus sequitur d

page.notes: Greek words in the first lines are set in a Greek font; accents transcribed as printed as far as legible. The word "puellus" and "pusio" and the diphthong line have some ink damage; "sequitur" followed by a catchword-like mark "d" at the foot, read as a catchword. Final "d" is the catchword.
